idea: RealityRouter
thesis: Outcome API routing a requested real-world result to human, agent, service, sensor, or robot.
best_wedge: Start as broker/orchestrator over existing human-field networks rather than recruiting a marketplace.
monetization: Per-task take rate; orchestration fee; enterprise SLA/API; verification add-ons; routing intelligence.
main_risks: Supply acquisition, liability, fraud, variable physical-world execution.

idea: Proof-of-Work / Reality Attestation
thesis: Neutral evidence and verification layer proving that a physical-world task or observation occurred.
best_wedge: Define proof schemas + capture SDK/API + verification scoring; integrate with existing task platforms.
monetization: Per-verification fee; enterprise subscriptions; fraud/risk API; evidence storage; compliance plans.
main_risks: Hard ground truth, device spoofing, privacy, evidentiary/legal claims.

idea: Human Escalation API
thesis: Fault-tolerance layer that lets agents summon human approval, judgment, or intervention when stuck.
best_wedge: Begin with asynchronous judgment/approval microtasks, not general labor.
monetization: Per escalation; seat + usage; premium latency SLA; vertical expert pools.
main_risks: HumanLayer-like approval plumbing exists; sourcing reliable humans and routing latency.

idea: Delegated Authority + Budget API
thesis: Policy engine answering whether an agent is authorized to act, spend, delegate, or escalate.
best_wedge: Complement Auth0/WorkOS/FIDO/AP2 rather than replace identity; own runtime decision semantics and budget controls.
monetization: Active agent pricing; authorization checks; spend-volume tiers; enterprise governance; audit/compliance.
main_risks: Crowded identity/auth market, standards moving quickly, enterprise security expectations.

idea: Work Receipt / Reputation Protocol
thesis: Portable signed receipts of completed work feeding evidence-grounded reputation across humans/agents/services.
best_wedge: Receipt first, reputation second. Bind task, principal, executor, evidence, outcome, cost and verifier.
monetization: Receipt issuance/verification; reputation API; enterprise audit; marketplace integrations; data licensing.
main_risks: Cold-start adoption, Sybil resistance, standard competition, counterparties need incentives to sign receipts.

idea: Proof Schema Registry for Agent Tasks
thesis: A registry of proof schemas that define what evidence is required for different types of agent tasks. Low competition, high utility, immediate value.
argument: Every marketplace needs to know what proof to collect. Defining proof schemas is a registry problem, not a marketplace problem. No existing standard.
best_wedge: Create open-source proof schema specification + hosted registry API
monetization: Free OSS schema + hosted registry API + enterprise compliance

idea: Agent Task Receipt Protocol (ATRP)
thesis: A standard protocol for issuing, verifying, and searching signed receipts of completed agent tasks. Builds on SCITT but adds task-specific structure.
argument: SCITT provides the cryptographic foundation but not the task-specific structure. ERC-8004 attempts on-chain but lacks grounded receipts. Need a middle layer.
best_wedge: Receipt SDK + schemas compatible with SCITT; issue/verify/search receipts
monetization: Free OSS SDK + hosted verification/search API + enterprise audit
main_risks: Standards convergence, adoption by existing marketplaces

idea: Evidence-Grounded Agent Capability Reputation
thesis: Reputation computed from grounded receipts, not ratings. Task-specific, evidence-backed capability scores.
argument: ERC-8004 analysis found reputation was a poor trust signal. Ratings lack grounding. Receipts provide verifiable evidence. This is the key differentiator.
best_wedge: Build reputation from receipts; task-specific scores
monetization: API pricing for reputation queries + enterprise audit

idea: AI Credits / Perks API — machine-readable database of every legitimate startup, student, developer, open-source and promotional compute programme
thesis: AI providers are throwing large quantities of credits at startups. WSJ reported founders receiving packages worth hundreds of thousands to millions. Normalize this.

idea: Agent Subscription Economics API — "unlimited" plans have weird quotas/subsidies, effective compute worth many multiples of subscription cost
thesis: Heavy users can consume dramatically more API-equivalent compute than subscription price. $200 plans worth many multiples under heavy usage.

idea: SameModel API — same open-weight model served by different providers is NOT the same product. Measure real differences.
thesis: 2026 measurement study found same model across providers differs by context, throughput, latency, reliability, pricing, protocol behavior.

idea: Search API Economics — actual economics of agent search: query price + downstream fetch/token cost + evidence yield
thesis: Search providers have similar accuracy but very different evidence economics. One API may cause agent to open far more pages.

idea: Sandbox Deals / Compute API — machine-readable economics/capabilities/free tiers for agent execution environments
thesis: Agent code execution is its own infrastructure category. E2B, Daytona, Modal, Upstash differ dramatically.

idea: Rate Limits + Quotas API — normalize RPM/TPM/RPD/concurrency/burst across all providers
thesis: All sophisticated agents still defeated by 429 TOO MANY REQUESTS. Rate limits change constantly.

idea: Model Availability / Deprecation API — endpoints constantly change, track new/preview/stable/deprecated/sunset/removed
thesis: Agents need to know: is every configured model still valid? Endpoints change constantly.

idea: API Billing Decoder — pricing formulas increasingly weird: per token, cached token, long-context surcharge, batch discount, priority surcharge
thesis: AI infrastructure pricing becoming incredibly difficult to normalize. One universal schema needed.

idea: Free-Tier Allocation Engine — spend free allowances optimally across providers
thesis: Agents have Gemini allowance, OpenRouter free models, Cloudflare allowance, signup credits, GPU credits, search credits.

idea: API Promotion Feed — LLMDeals generalized beyond inference to search/browser/sandbox/GPU/vector/speech/OCR
thesis: Generalize LLM Deals into AgentDeals. Track all agent resource promotions.

idea: Coding Agent Deals API — Cursor/Codex/Claude/OpenCode economics, plan/model/usage-multiplier/quota/promotion
thesis: Research evaluates cloud coding agents on true cost of ownership, cache economics and defect-repair burden.

idea: Agent Infrastructure Credits API — GPU/browser/search/sandbox/vector credits normalized
thesis: Credit market large enough to matter. Providers using massive subsidies strategically.

idea: Agent Browser Compatibility Index — site × browser-provider reliability data
thesis: Managed agent-browser market has competing providers with different pricing/features.

idea: Provider Feature Reality — probe actual capabilities vs docs: streaming, tool-choice, JSON schema, context limits
thesis: Docs say OpenAI-compatible but truth differs operationally. Generate original measurements.

idea: Cache Economics API — expected uncached/cached cost, break-even reuse, best provider for caching
thesis: 99.3% prompt-cache hit rate and 88.6% reduction in realized API cost observed in enterprise coding-agent study.

idea: AgentDeals — broaden LLMDeals into search/GPU/browser/sandbox/API discounts and credits
thesis: Simplest expansion path: LLMDeals becoming AgentDeals.
